name: _is_zerotensor
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_is_zerotensor(Tensor self) -> bool. This representative signature is NOT exclusive. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: "aten::_is_zerotensor(Tensor self) -> bool". The original Gems pytest owns the full contract: overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation; do not narrow its coverage to this representative signature, remove workloads, or adapt reference behavior to fit it. Semantics derived from the tests: a host-side metadata query that reads the ZeroTensor dispatch marker of the tensor impl and returns a Python bool (type res is bool, not a 0-dim tensor). It is not an element-wise zero test: an ordinary dense torch.zeros operand is reported False and only an aten._efficientzerotensor operand is reported True. Cheap rewrites of a flagged operand (identity, detach, slice, view, reshape, transpose, unsqueeze, narrow, expand, contiguous) preserve the marker, while materializing ops (clone, zeros_like) drop it. The query must not materialize, detach or otherwise rewrite its operand (shape, stride, storage_offset, device and dtype are unchanged). None is a valid undefined-tensor operand for the native operator. The schema takes a single Tensor, so non-tensor arguments (int, float, str, list, tuple, dict, dtype) and a missing argument must raise RuntimeError or TypeError; there is no unsupported-dtype or unsupported-rank form to reject. The result is a Python bool with no grad_fn, so there is no backward workload, but grad-requiring operands are accepted and left with requires_grad True. Only one overload is registered, so no additional scalar/list overloads are involved; error and invalid-argument behavior remains asserted in the original pytest.
